text:
mike_chen: Quick sync — I ran an end-to-end comparison between our replay harness and the synthetic loader using the same 8k prompt set. On nv4x2 with kernel=v2.3.4 the replay run has ~9% worse p50 decode latency. Configs were identical (seeded RNG, same decoding params). Anyone seen this delta before?

zeynep: Can you paste the exact commands/configs you used? small config mismatch (batching, stop sequences) can explain differences.

mike_chen: Sure — pasted below. Both runs used batch=8, per-request max_new_tokens=128, temp=0.0, top_p=0.95, stop=["\n\n"].

```
# replay
./replay_harness --trace traces/2025-prod-sample.jsonl \
  --model redwood/falcon-7b \
  --decoding '{"temp":0.0,"top_p":0.95,"stop":["\\n\\n"]}' \
  --kernel-profile kernel:v2.3.4 \
  --batch 8 --seed 42 --out replay_results.jsonl

# synthetic
./synthetic_loader --num-reqs 8000 --prompt-file prompts/8k.txt \
  --model redwood/falcon-7b \
  --decoding '{"temp":0.0,"top_p":0.95,"stop":["\\n\\n"]}' \
  --batch 8 --seed 42 --out synth_results.jsonl
```

mike_chen: I also grabbed kernel-level profiling. Short excerpt:

```
# replay (p50 aggregate)
attention_kernel: 4.12ms
ff_kernel: 1.28ms
kv_cache_lookup: 0.64ms
io+dispatch: 1.86ms
total_decode_per_request: 11.90ms
kv_hit_rate: 71.8%\n
# synthetic (p50 aggregate)
attention_kernel: 3.87ms
ff_kernel: 1.20ms
kv_cache_lookup: 0.42ms
io+dispatch: 1.70ms
total_decode_per_request: 10.95ms
kv_hit_rate: 88.5%
```

zeynep: Hmm kv_hit_rate difference stands out — replay traces might have longer prefix overlap patterns, causing more random access and cache churn. Did you run with the same KV cache settings (max_entries, shard_size)?

mike_chen: Yes, same kv config (kv_max_entries=1e6, shard_size=64). I think the trace characteristics (many short completions with overlapping prefixes) cause more frequent partial KV invalidations in the replay harness.

samir: Also double-check tokenizer alignment. I instrumented token counts for the first 200 prompts and found ~2% more tokens in the replay run. Small tokenizer mismatches -> longer decode -> more KV entries -> lower kv_hit_rate. Reproducer below.

```
# quick tokenizer repro (python)
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('redwood-falcon-tokenizer.json')
text = "Café — test: normalize?"
print('raw len:', len(text))
print('token_count:', len(tok.encode(text).tokens))
# observed: replay_path token_count=17, synthetic token_count=16
```

samir: The difference was because the replay loader preserves original Unicode (em-dash U+2014) while the synthetic generator normalizes to ascii '-' earlier in the pipeline. NFKC + strip-zero-width chars fixed alignment for us.

katie: Good catch. Also check stop-sequence matching: if replay uses string stop matching and synth uses token-level stop detection, you'll get different effective truncation points. We should standardize on token-level stop detection for apples-to-apples.

mike_chen: Agreed. For this investigation I re-ran with a normalization step and token-level stop checking. Results: p50 gap dropped to ~1.8% and kv_hit_rate equalized to ~87%. Kernel times then matched within noise.

katie: Can you add the normalization + token-stop flow as a flag in both harnesses? e.g. `--normalize "NFKC" --stop-mode token` so future comparisons are deterministic.

zeynep: Also propose adding a KV-hit metric per-request to the profiler (histogram) and an eviction trace for the ~1% worst requests so we can pinpoint churn patterns.

mike_chen: Will do. Action items:
- mike_chen: add NFKC normalization and token-level stop flag to replay harness (PR coming).
- zeynep: add per-request kv_hit_rate histogram + eviction trace to kernel profiler.
- samir: run a focused 50k prompt replay with/without normalization to validate fix at scale.
- katie: update the apples-to-apples checklist in docs (encoding, normalization, stop-mode, kernel version, batch size).

deploy-bot: perf-alert created: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/7891 — benchmark job flagged when p50 regression >5% vs baseline kernel:v2.3.2.

mike_chen: Thanks — I'll send the PR and rerun the 8k tests once profiler changes are in. :thumbsup:

zeynep: Thanks — good find. Small text-normalization differences are deceptively expensive.
